subject: On-call + SLA bundle — terms, tiers, and final counteroffer
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan@acmecloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: SLA options + on-call coverage questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're evaluating Redwood for a critical service path and need clarity on a couple of things before procurement will greenlight the pilot:

- Can you share the exact uptime tiers (monthly SLA %) and how outage credits are calculated?
- What does 24/7 on-call actually include — paging, escalation matrix, guaranteed engineer response time?
- Are there price breaks for a 12–24 month committed capacity or a multi-year enterprise discount?

Procurement has asked for a concise quote and any standard add-on fees (e.g., escalation retainer). Can you send a one-page option set we can circulate?

Appreciate it —
Jordan
Director of Infrastructure
ACME Cloud
[attachment: none]
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T11:00:00-05:00
Subject: Re: SLA options + on-call coverage questions

Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the clear list. We have three packaged options that customers commonly evaluate; I attached a short PDF with the table (Redwood_SLA_Tiers_v1.pdf). High-level here:

1) Standard — 99.5% monthly uptime, business-hours support (M–F, 9–5 local), 8-hour initial response for Sev2, 24-hour for Sev1; 0% credits under minor incidents, standard pricing.

2) Enhanced — 99.9% monthly uptime, extended support (M–F, 8–20 local), 2-hour response for Sev2, 1-hour for Sev1, limited weekend coverage; 5% monthly credit threshold.

3) Priority (Premium) — 99.95% monthly uptime, 24/7 on-call with a dedicated escalation path, 15-minute paging for Sev1, 1-hour for Sev2, and a named escalation engineer on rotation. This includes access to our priority-runbook queue and quarterly on-call runbook reviews. Typically sold with a reserved capacity commitment.

On pricing: we can offer a stepped discount for committed Dedicated capacity — 10% for 12 months, 15% for 24 months — subject to minimum monthly commit. An escalation retainer (one-time setup + monthly fee) covers guaranteed on-call contact and faster escalation routing.

If you can share expected QPS and token volume, I can tailor the pricing and include an example monthly cost.

Attached: Redwood_SLA_Tiers_v1.pdf (1 page) — quick comparison table + stub pricing bands.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123
From: Jordan Park <jordan@acmecloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-11-21T08:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: SLA options + on-call coverage questions

Grace —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the PDF. A few follow-ups from procurement and our SRE team:

- For Priority: we need 24/7 paging and a guaranteed engineering response (not just an acknowledgment). Is the 15-minute paging a guaranteed live-engineer acknowledgement or an automated alert followed by triage within 15 minutes?
- Credits: procurement is pushing to have a minimum credit floor (i.e., monthly credits can't exceed X% of the invoice) — any flexibility there?
- Pricing: 10% on 12 months is a good start. Would Redwood budge to 12% or 15% on a 12-month commit if we agree to a rolling monthly commit size and a joint SLA review at 6 months?

Cc'ing procurement — please add any MFT/PO requirements.

—Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@acmecloud.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA options + on-call coverage questions — counteroffer

Hi Jordan —

Appreciate the follow-ups. I wanted to jump in with a concrete counter so your procurement team has something to work with. Summary of what we can do for ACME Cloud on Priority tier:

- 24/7 paging = guaranteed live-engineer acknowledgment within 15 minutes for Sev1 (not an auto-bot ack). Our runbook requires a triage update within 60 minutes and ongoing updates until resolution.
- Credit floor: we can cap outage credits at 30% of the monthly committed spend for extreme events; normal incident credits follow the SLA table in the attachment.
- Pricing concession: 12% discount for a 12-month committed Dedicated capacity with a quarterly joint SLA review at month 3 and month 9. If ACME opts for a 24-month commit we can extend to 17% discount and waive the one-time escalation retainer.
- Escalation retainer: normally $7,500 one-time + $2,000/mo for named escalation routing. With a 12-month commit we can reduce the retainer to $3,500 one-time + $1,200/mo.

Attached is a counter document with the exact language we propose for the SLA (SLA_Redwood_Counter_20261122.pdf). If procurement can accept those credit caps and the 12% concession we can prepare an order form and DocuSign envelope this week.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales (Enterprise)
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
[attachment: SLA_Redwood_Counter_20261122.pdf]
From: Jordan Park <jordan@acmecloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-11-30T16:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: SLA options + on-call coverage questions — counteroffer

Team —

Appreciate the responsiveness and the concessions. Procurement and SRE have reviewed Karthik's counter. We're generally OK with the 12% on a 12-month commit with the reduced retainer, but two remaining asks before we route to PO:

1) During business hours (our core hours M–F 08:00–18:00 ET) we need a 30-minute SLA for Sev1 acknowledgements instead of 15 minutes, with 15 minutes retained for true production-impacting incidents only. This reflects our internal alerting patterns and will reduce false-positive escalations.
2) Can the credit cap be lowered to 25% of committed spend for the first three months, then revert to 30%? Procurement wants a slightly smaller initial exposure while we ramp.

If Redwood can accept those two tweaks we can get a PO issued by next week and push the order to legal/DocuSign.

Jordan Park
Director of Infrastructure
ACME Cloud
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@acmecloud.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-11-30T17:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: SLA options + on-call coverage questions — counteroffer

Jordan —

Thanks — we can agree to both asks:

- Business-hours Sev1 acknowledgement at 30 minutes (we'll keep 15 minutes for incidents that match our production-impact definition; we'll include precise criteria in the redline).
- Credit cap at 25% of committed spend for months 1–3, then 30% thereafter.

I'll produce the redline to Karthik's counter and prepare the DocuSign envelope (link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-ACME-SLA-2026). I can also set up a 30-minute call tomorrow if procurement wants to walk the final language.

Next steps:
- I will upload the redline to the HubSpot deal (link included) and kick DocuSign.
- Once PO/PO number is in, we will finalize start date and reserved capacity sizing.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
